caption:
Menu in another language? Point your phone's camera at it and Google Translate shows it in English, right on your screen.

Why it works: the Translate app reads the words through your camera and swaps in your language on the spot. Since 2019, camera translations run on Google's neural machine translation, a kind of AI.

How:
1. Open the Google Translate app (free on Android and iPhone).
2. Set "From" to Detect language and "To" to English.
3. Tap Camera, under the text box.
4. Point it at the menu, sign or label. Tap the shutter to freeze it.

The catch: small, blurry or fancy lettering may come out wrong, so check anything that matters (allergies: ask the staff). Going somewhere without data? Download the language in the app before you leave so it works offline.

Privacy tip: point it at menus and signs, not at your passport, bank cards or letters with your address.

Do this: Open Google Translate. Tap Camera. Point.
Send this to the friend you're travelling with.
The menu is drawn and made up for this post. The feature is real.
Follow to learn one real AI trick a day.

caption:
Group chat chaos? Get the list. Paste the family dinner chat into AI and ask who's bringing what.

Why it works: the AI only reads what you paste, so the list comes straight from those messages. Claude sorted 7 messages into what's covered, what's still missing and the one question waiting for me. Its real reply is on screen, word for word (its last suggestion line is cut).

How:
1. In your chat app, copy the messages (just the text).
2. Open ChatGPT, Claude or Gemini.
3. Paste them and type: "Tell me who's bringing what, what's still missing, and what I need to reply to. Keep it short." Add your first name so it knows which questions are yours.

The catch: it only sees the messages you paste. Miss one and the list misses it too, so check it against the chat before you reply.

Privacy tip: copy just the messages, not a screenshot full of phone numbers, and leave out addresses or anything private.

Do this: Paste the chat. Ask: who's bringing what?
Send this to whoever always ends up organizing.
The chat is made up for this post. Real run in Claude, Oct 27 2026.
